title: Sita found
hook: how do you speak to a frightened captive from a tree without making her scream? Hanuman thinks it through, and then tells her a story

segments.voice: Yesterday: the ashoka grove, part two. Ravana's offer, a blade of grass, and a deadline of two months. Did you say a quiet, plain no? Today, Hanuman has to speak. Day six hundred eighteen.

Ravana has gone. The guards have finished threatening her and drawn back. Sita sits alone at the foot of the tree, worn out, close to the end of hope. Hanuman is right above her. He has found her. And now he faces a delicate problem of a different kind. A monkey suddenly dropping out of a tree and talking, in the middle of the enemy's garden, could terrify her. If she cries out, the guards wake, and everything is lost.
screen: `SITA, ALONE, NEAR THE END OF HOPE.` → `HANUMAN, RIGHT ABOVE HER.` → `ONE CRY AND IT'S LOST.`

segments.voice: So once again Valmiki lets us listen to Hanuman think. If I speak to her in polished Sanskrit, he reasons, the way a learned priest would, she'll think I'm Ravana in disguise. Ravana has already fooled her once, dressed as a holy man. That's how he took her. So I'll speak in plain, everyday language, the speech of ordinary people, and every word will mean something. And I won't start with myself. I'll start with Rama. And then he does something beautiful. He doesn't call out to her. He doesn't announce himself. Softly, from the branches, he begins to tell a story, as if to no one. There was a king called Dasharatha, he says, righteous and great. His eldest son Rama was sent into the forest with his wife and his brother. In the forest, his wife Sita was carried off. Rama searched for her, made friends with the monkey king Sugriva, and sent monkeys in every direction to find her. And I, he says, crossed the ocean, and I have seen her. That's all. A story told quietly in the dark, about her own life, by someone who obviously loves the person she loves. Look at the order he chose. He lets her hear her husband's name before she hears anything frightening. He lets her recognize her own story before she sees the teller. He gives her the chance to come toward the voice, instead of having it come at her. Sita, at the foot of the tree, lifts her head.
screen: `NOT PRIESTLY SANSKRIT.` · `PLAIN SPEECH, AND RAMA FIRST.` · `A STORY TOLD SOFTLY TO NO ONE.` · then, large: `SITA LIFTS HER HEAD.`

segments.voice: Sit and settle. Think of someone you need to approach about something delicate. Before you plan what to say, ask what they'd most need to hear first. Not your point, but something that tells them they're safe: a name they love, something you share, a memory. Let that first sentence form gently. You don't have to say it yet. Just breathe with it, quietly. The bell holds the time.
Sita found. Hanuman, above her in the tree, chooses plain speech and tells Rama's story softly, so that the first thing Sita hears is the name she loves.
Your line: Rama's name first. Today, when you bring someone hard or surprising news, begin with something that tells them they're safe. Day six hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: Some teachers of the Sundara Kanda point to Hanuman's choice of plain speech and his soft retelling of Rama's story as a model of how to speak with care.

original.note: Sanskrit mānuṣī vāk, human (ordinary) speech: what Hanuman decides to use.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hanuman just found Sita and said hello.
what it means: he plans every detail so she won't be frightened or cry out.
what a scholar hears: Hanuman's debate over which register of speech to use, refined Sanskrit or common speech, is one of the epic's notable reflections on language and audience.

notes: Hanuman's reasoning about Sanskrit 'like a twice-born' vs. 'human speech' (mānuṣī vāk): confirm Sundara 30 and the exact term for the register he chooses; scholars debate what it implies.
Sita 'close to the end of hope': Sundara 26–28 includes her thoughts of ending her life; the script deliberately does not detail this. Confirm.
Ravana's earlier disguise as a mendicant (Aranya Kanda): referenced as 'dressed as a holy man'.
Order: Trijata's dream (Sundara 27) and the omens (29) are not included in these days; a Keeper may want them mentioned.
Fresh review: 'dozed off' changed to 'drawn back' (whether the guards sleep here is unconfirmed); cut 'the most delicate problem of the whole journey'; softened howItsDone claims.
